svg.text: G — Readiness review → plugin generation
Runbook §36.1 and §36.2 as one flow, because §36.2 cannot start without a completed §36.1 at the current version.
§36.1 Design Readiness Review
1 · Choose mode
full — all §34 checklist items. incremental — only items whose
sections changed since the last review's baseline version, per git diff.
2 · Mechanical checks — always run in full
scripts/validate-workflow-catalog.py
scripts/validate-vocabulary.py
scripts/check-spec-version.py
scripts/validate-content.py
scripts/validate-workflow-specs.py
scripts/validate-skills.py
All six must pass.
Mode does not exempt
them.
3 · Verify the §34 checklist over the whole document set
spec · runbook · revision history · workflow-catalog.yaml · vocabulary.yaml
file-skeletons.yaml · setup-interview.md · workflow-specs/*
design-spec/content/* · design-spec/sync-exclusions.md
4 · One issue list
Completeness, safety, and consistency findings. The list gates finalization.
An open tenet-check exclusion in sync-exclusions.md is a finding here (§34).
5 · resolve, repeat 2–4
Each spec change made to clear a finding
is itself Proceed-gated. Loop until clean.
Findings open
→ not ready
6 · Finalize — clean pass
Add a revision-history row. Confirm status: design_ready_for_generation
across the stamped set.
Increment openaos_version only if the specification itself changed.
§36.2 Plugin Generation
1 · Precondition
A completed §36.1 review at the current openaos_version.
2 · Render — with the baseline guard
Read §28, render every §35 source into claude-plugin/openaos/
Before each skills/*/SKILL.md: compare it against the recorded
baseline (sync-state.py check). Matches → regenerate as normal.
Differs → an unreflected hand-edit: stop, name the file, and send
the user to §36.3, which must run first (§33).
content/ and workflow-specs/ render unconditionally — they are
copies, and §36.3 has already run.
3 · Preview, then Proceed
Two separate lists: files to be created, and existing files that
would be overwritten. Generate only on the exact word.
4 · Validate the result
· plugin.json well-formed; name and version == openaos_version
· the three SKILL.md files pass validate-skills.py (SK1–SK5)
· spec citations resolve; each skill cites its governing §8/§12/§13
· in-skill file references resolve; the Proceed gate is present
· workflow-specs/ byte-identical — validate-workflow-specs.py (WS1–WS2)
· content/ byte-identical to design-spec/content/ — validate-content.py
· marketplace.json source points at ./claude-plugin/openaos
· no live reference to the retired status-report-template.md
· every report-producing workflow points at a real HTML template
· every such template opens standalone — CSS inline, no external assets
5 · Record · 6 · Re-baseline
Add a revision-history row for the completed generation.
No version increment unless the packaged framework changed.
Then python scripts/sync-state.py record — the baseline the
next guard and the next §36.3 both read.
Three things this flow is telling you
· For content/ and workflow-specs/, spec → plugin is a copy. The byte-identical checks exist so the plugin can never quietly diverge from
the spec. Hand-edit a file there and CI fails the pull request — that is exactly what stops an unreflected edit from reaching main.
· skills/ is different — it is authored prose, so there is no byte-identity to assert. A hand-edit there is not clobbered and not ignored: the
baseline guard stops the generation and sends you to §36.3, which reflects the edit into §8.1/§12/§13 before the plugin is rendered again.
· The version increments in §36.1, not §36.2. Generation packages a version; it does not create one.
